# attacktree

> attacktree is a free, browser-based editor for attack trees and decision trees. You describe how an attacker (or a failure) could reach a goal in a small YAML format, or draw it on a canvas, and attacktree lays it out as a diagram. It is local-first: trees are saved in the browser and share links carry the whole tree in the URL fragment. Built and maintained by LESIS (https://lesis.lat), a security engineering team.

The format is the Deciduous YAML format (https://www.deciduous.app/), extended with an optional `positions` section. Files written for Deciduous open unchanged.

## Docs

- [Full documentation](llms-full.txt): Markdown. Concepts, the complete YAML reference, modeling patterns, a step-by-step method, the canvas, editor and diagnostics reference, sharing and exporting, and an FAQ.
- [Documentation (HTML)](docs/): the same content, with live diagrams.
- [JSON Schema](attacktree.schema.json): the tree format as a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12).

## Format in brief

```yaml
title: Account takeover
facts:                      # true statements about the system
- public_api: The login API is on the internet
  from:
  - reality                 # implicit root node
attacks:                    # attacker actions
- stuffing: Credential stuffing on /login
  from:
  - public_api: via a botnet  # optional edge label
mitigations:                # defenses that counter an attack
- rate_limit: Rate limiting and breached-password checks
  from:
  - stuffing:
    implemented: false      # planned, not in place yet
goals:                      # what the attacker ultimately wants
- takeover: Take over a customer account
  from:
  - stuffing
```

- A node is a list item whose first key is its id (unique, `[A-Za-z_][\w-]*`) and whose value is its label.
- `from` lists the ids the node comes from. Arrows point from them to it.
- An edge entry is an id, or a map whose first key is the id, followed by flags at the same indentation: `backwards: true` (a mitigation sends the attacker back to an earlier step) and `implemented: false` (planned).
- `filter: [ids]` shows only the paths through those nodes. `positions: {id: [x, y]}` stores nodes placed by hand.
- Model in a rhythm: an attack, the mitigation that counters it, then the attacker's next move because of that mitigation.
- Gaps are found automatically: an attack with no implemented mitigation is marked "No defense", and a goal reachable without beating any defense is an "Open path" (drawn in red). No `#yolosec` labels are needed.

## Optional

- [Deciduous](https://www.deciduous.app/): the original tool by Ryan Petrich and Kelly Shortridge, where this format comes from.
- [LESIS](https://lesis.lat): the team behind attacktree. Security assessments, security consultancy, due diligence and custom tools.
